patch.value: A context read's output cursor was refused as stale on an unchanged tracker in one full coverage run (read_output_cursor_stale on the low_level collection)

Observed once on 2026-11-22 in a local full coverage run (980 files, about 16 minutes, host under load): tests/integration/read-output/composed-continuation.integration.spec.ts failed at its context loop. The replay 'pm --json context --limit 25 --output-budget 1500 --tag matrix --output-cursor <cursor>' was refused with read_output_cursor_stale; the decoded cursor names command context, path low_level, offset 3, count 24. No test step writes to the tracker between issuing the cursor and replaying it. The same spec passed in the full non-coverage run of the same tree and in three isolated runs (17 to 19 s each); under coverage it ran 24.8 s. Hypothesis, not verified: a context row carries a field derived from the wall clock (a recency or age bucket), so a slow replay that crosses a bucket boundary rebuilds a different row and the complete-row fingerprint no longer matches. Only health declares a fingerprint policy that ignores volatile fields.

The cause is identified by reproducing the refusal deterministically, for example with a controlled clock between the first page and the replay; If a wall-clock-derived field is the cause, the context fingerprint excludes it through a declared continuation fingerprint policy or the field is made stable for a cursor's lifetime, and a spec replays a cursor across the boundary; If the cause is a test-fixture interaction instead, the spec is isolated and this item records the evidence
A cursor issued by a context read is accepted on replay while the tracker is unchanged
One replay under load was refused with read_output_cursor_stale although no write intervened

value.text: Duplicate check: pm search for 'read_output_cursor_stale context cursor flaky' returned the closed GH-1753 item (intent reads, fixed by binding cursors to first-pass rows) and the closed health replay isolation item pm-oahhyc; neither covers a plain context read going stale without a write.
